Reason: The serial chest X-rays (Figures 1a-1c) demonstrate a cystic lesion in the right lung that has increased in size over time, indicating slow growth since 1988. The linear structure visible within the cyst (indicated by arrows in Figure 1b) represents a dilated intracystic vein, a characteristic finding often associated with pulmonary sequestration or similar congenital anomalies where systemic venous drainage is prominent.
